tasks.title: Promote the three staged base-logic migrations
tasks.dod: The three staged migrations are promoted to migrations/0002–0004 (next free numbers) and applied by the test harness; an integration test proves the tables, the index and one-row-per-chat upsert.

tasks.title: Parse the city query and recognise countries
tasks.dod: Table-driven unit tests show parseCityQuery returns blank / too_long / unknown_country / {name, countryCode?} for every edge row, and countries.ts resolves codes, names and the USA/UK aliases.

tasks.title: Pick the best-matching populated place and format its name
tasks.dod: Unit tests show pickBestMatch keeps only populated places, picks the highest population (ties and missing population → source order), flags ambiguity, and formatPlaceName drops a missing region.

tasks.title: Encode the lookup limits and UTC counting keys
tasks.dod: Unit tests at the boundaries (4,999/5,000 daily; 29/30 per chat; both hit → daily_limit) and for the UTC day key and the 60-minute window start pass.

tasks.title: Describe and round the current weather reading
tasks.dod: Unit tests show WMO codes map to words with an "unknown conditions" fallback, all four numbers round to whole numbers (no "-0"), and the reading time renders in the Home city's timezone.

tasks.title: Declare the four new ports and the get-home-city use case
tasks.dod: ports.ts declares PlaceLookup, WeatherProvider, HomeCityRepo and UsageCounter over domain types; a unit test with a fake repo shows getHomeCity returns the chat's Place or none.

tasks.title: Implement the set-home-city use case
tasks.dod: Unit tests with fake ports show: parse errors and both limits make no reserve and no lookup; an allowed request reserves exactly once before the lookup; only a found place is saved; not_found/unavailable carry the current Home city.

tasks.title: Implement the get-current-weather use case
tasks.dod: Unit tests with fake ports show: no Home city → no_home_city with no counting; a limit hit → no reserve, no fetch; an allowed request reserves once then fetches at the stored coordinates; a provider failure → unavailable.

tasks.title: Implement the D1 HomeCityRepo and UsageCounter adapters
tasks.dod: Integration tests on the local D1 show: save replaces per chat and never touches another chat; region NULL round-trips as undefined; counts honour the strict 60-minute window and a missing day row reads 0; reserve increments, inserts and prunes in one batch.

tasks.title: Implement the Open-Meteo geocoding and forecast adapters
tasks.dod: Unit tests with a stubbed fetch and recorded fixtures show: geocoding maps results to PlaceCandidates (English names, feature code, population, optional region) and passes the country filter; forecast maps current fields to CurrentWeather; timeout, network error, non-OK or malformed JSON → unavailable.

tasks.title: Build the Telegram edge: request-log middleware, chat-type split, start, help and group replies
tasks.dod: Integration tests through the webhook show: every accepted update writes exactly one `update` log event (including a thrown handler, which still gets the fault reply and a 200); edits get no reply; the bot's own command in a group gets the private-chat pointer while other group traffic and channel posts get nothing; /start names the Home city when set; anything else gets the help list.

tasks.title: Add the /city command and its replies
tasks.dod: Integration tests through the webhook (stubbed Open-Meteo + Telegram fetch, local D1) show the spec'd reply for every set-city outcome (ok, ambiguous hint, blank, too long, not found, unknown country, unavailable with "still …", user_limit, daily_limit), the stored row after each, and the log event's outcome and lookups.

tasks.title: Add the /weather command and its replies
tasks.dod: Integration tests through the webhook show the spec'd reply for ok (all fields, rounded, local reading time), no Home city (no fetch), source down/slow, user_limit and daily_limit, and the log event carries outcome, lookups and reading_time.

tasks.title: Build the bot once per isolate and verify the per-message budgets end to end
tasks.dod: worker.ts builds adapters, use cases and the Bot once per isolate (cached at module scope, nothing per-request cached) and warns once when BOT_INFO is absent; e2e tests show ≤ 1 lookup + 1 reply per scenario, exactly one update event each, two chats isolated, and a hanging source still answered.

tasks.title: Update the README for the new commands and the BOT_INFO deploy step
tasks.dod: README lists /start, /city <name> and /weather with examples, the status line no longer says skeleton-only, the Deploy section includes `wrangler secret put BOT_INFO` as required for production, and `prettier --check` passes.

tasks.title: Resolve non-Latin set-city queries with a localized search and an English re-fetch
tasks.dod: Unit + contract tests show: a Latin query makes one language=en search; a non-Latin query searches in its script language (Cyrillic → uk), then re-fetches the picked place by id in English; each call is limit-checked and reserved; the reply name is English; the lookup count reaches the handler.

tasks.title: Record the two-lookup non-Latin set-city decision in ADR-0003 and the design docs
tasks.dod: Feature ADR-0003 (Accepted) records the localized search + English re-fetch, its cost (at most 2 lookups + 1 reply) and the Ukrainian-only Cyrillic limitation (OQ-4); sad.md §4/§5/§8 and the spec test-plan edge row say at most 2 lookups; prettier clean.

tasks.title: Pin the 1.5 s cutoff and tolerate malformed geocoder entries and unknown timezones
tasks.dod: A test asserts every outbound call uses AbortSignal.timeout(1500); `find` skips malformed entries and entries whose timezone Intl rejects, keeping the valid ones, and is `unavailable` only when the body/results are malformed or every entry is bad; `findById` with an unknown timezone is `unavailable`; npm test, lint, typecheck green.

tasks.title: Name the current Home city on every "couldn't find that place" reply
tasks.dod: `too_long` and `unknown_country` carry the current Home city (one D1 read, still no lookup and no limit read); the reply adds "Your city is still X." when one is set; `blank` is unchanged; npm test, lint, typecheck green.

tasks.title: Drop forged updates silently and fail closed without a webhook secret
tasks.dod: A wrong or missing secret header gets a bare 200 with no reason text and no bot work; an empty WEBHOOK_SECRET refuses every update (logged `startup_error`) instead of accepting all; SAD flow A wording matches spec §6.1; npm test, lint, typecheck green.

tasks.title: Keep the real outcome when the reply fails, name the fault, and prove no secret is logged
tasks.dod: A failing sendMessage sets `reply_failed: true`, keeps the handler's outcome and sends no second reply; a handler fault logs `fault` plus a secret-free `fault_kind`; a unit test of the collector covers ok, expected failure, fault and reply failure; an integration test over not_found, unavailable and storage fault asserts neither BOT_TOKEN nor WEBHOOK_SECRET in any log line; npm test, lint, typecheck green.

tasks.title: Let the get-current-weather use case report its lookups
tasks.dod: `getCurrentWeather(chatId, onLookup)` calls `onLookup` once per reserved lookup; the /weather handler counts through it instead of hard-coding; npm test, lint, typecheck green.

tasks.title: Use the real command in the help reply and assert nothing is stored where the plan says so
tasks.dod: The help reply says "send /city followed by the city name" (asserted); the edit, lookup-hang and daily-limit tests assert the Home city is unchanged; npm test, lint, typecheck green.
